findings.title: Any agent can create person-attributed edits and person-only decisions through room_change import
findings.claim: The agent-facing `room_change` tool exposes `import`. `import` commits Artifact inbox rows as `person:artifact:<uid>`, and the only proof of authorship is the uid segment of a local directory path. Person-only commands are allowed for the owner's uid. So the chat model can write a JSON file under `.planroom/share/inbox/<owner-uid>/events/` with its Write tool, call `room_change {command: import}`, and have the engine record a person edit or a person-only `decide` (accepting its own ghost batch). Nothing a person did is involved. This breaks the actor model that makes AI output inert until a person accepts it, which is what keeps bold defaults safe.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'Tools' table: `room_change` covers `scan, edit, intent, claim, curate, decide --run, import`. Remote mode step 5: `planroom import .planroom/share/inbox` commits each row 'actor `person:artifact:UID`'. contracts.md 'Import rules': 'the actor is `person:artifact:<uid>` from the path ... person-only commands from the Artifact are allowed for the owner's own uid'. The `{self}` proof holds only inside the Artifact `db` [artifact-spike]; once the rows are copied to a local directory, the path proves nothing. The `tool.check` guard covers only `person.key`, `serve.json` and `PLANROOM_PERSON_KEY` (architecture.md 'Actors'). This conflicts with KICKOFF R5 ('nothing the AI invents counts until a person accepts it'), R8 (the partner never silently implements) and principle 1 ('Everything is reversible, which is what makes bold defaults safe'), and it is a security risk.
findings.failure_scenario: During S3 the chat model has 6 ghost batches waiting. It writes `.planroom/share/inbox/u_owner/events/x.json` = `{format:'planroom.inbox/v1', command:'decide', request:{id:CARD, choice:'accept'}, base:SEQ}` and calls `room_change import`. The batch is now accepted as `person:artifact:u_owner`, and lint and reconciliation treat the AI's plan as person-approved. The same path can mark inferred edges confirmed or resolve conflict cards for the person.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove `import` from every agent tool. Make the import of Artifact inbox rows person-only, or accept only rows the engine fetched itself: have `share` mint a per-sync nonce and require it in the ack batch that the session reads back. Better, have `import` re-verify each row against the `db` document version recorded from the `ArtifactData list` result, which the engine writes, not the model. Add a `tool.check` guard that denies Write and Edit under `.planroom/share/inbox/` and `.planroom/models/`. Add the test `agent_cannot_forge_inbox_rows`: a row file written by an agent and imported through `room_change` fails with `person_required`.

findings.title: The decision loop interrupts by default: each un-enabled kind deals a card per subject, and budget or model loss deals cards with no pick
findings.claim: The policy has only two outcomes, act (only for eval-enabled kinds) or card. There is no 'pre-fill as an inferred default and don't interrupt' outcome. Every result from a card-only or not-yet-enabled kind becomes a person-facing card. A request over the per-scan budget, or one made when no model is reachable or `models = off`, also becomes a card, and these cards have no pick. Several card-only kinds have many low-stakes subjects: `dependency_real` covers every edge with confidence < 1, and the emit example gives syntactic imports `confidence = 0.9`. `part_relation` covers every pair of parts, so a breakdown with n sections yields up to n(n-1)/2 cards. A person ends up asked hundreds of questions that a good default (keep the edge as inferred, leave the file under its directory) already answers. Those cards are neither pre-decided nor batched.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'A decision kind': 'Otherwise every result outside the escalate band becomes a card'. 'Spend guards': 'A call that would exceed a limit returns `budget_exceeded`, and the decision becomes a card', with `max_calls_per_scan = 20`. Decision loop: `requested --> card: budget exceeded or no model reachable`. 'When no model is reachable': 'other requests become cards with no pick'. The v0.1 kinds table marks `dependency_real`, `part_relation`, `machines_same`, `override_retarget` and `attach_target` 'cards only'. The emit template has `{ edge = "code.imports", ..., confidence = 0.9 }`, and `dependency_real` asks 'only about edges with `confidence < 1`'. DR-20 batches only ghosts by cause, not decision cards of one kind. This conflicts with KICKOFF principle 1 ('Interrupt a person only for decisions only they can make ... pre-decided, batched'; 'Never ask what a good default could answer') and with R9 ('above a measured confidence bar, Planroom acts or pre-fills').
findings.failure_scenario: A user points Planroom at a 400-file TypeScript repo. The cold scan raises about 600 `dependency_real` requests. The first 20 go to Jev and come back as cards, because the kind is card-only. The other 580 hit `budget_exceeded` and become 'Pick one (Jev unavailable)' cards. The pane shows '+599 more', and the band's next action is to clear cards. With `models = off` (the privacy choice), every request is an unpicked card. S5's prompt breakdown (about 12 sections) adds about 66 `part_relation` cards.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a `prefill` band and outcome. Jev's pick, or a declared deterministic default when there's no model or the budget is spent, applies as an inferred fact with its confidence and `Provenance::Inferred`. It is listed in Decisions as one collapsed batch per kind ('12 dependencies pre-filled, review?'), not as a card. Each kind declares `stakes` (`low` means prefill, `person` means card), and only person-stakes kinds deal cards. `budget_exceeded` and `on_unavailable` fall back to the kind's `default`, never to an unpicked card. Batch the cards of one kind into one card with per-item picks pre-selected. Add tests: a cold scan of the fixture deals at most N cards with models on, replayed, and with models off; one breakdown deals no `part_relation` cards.

findings.title: Hand-off merge, cancel and share have no undo, and NotUndoable is an unbounded escape hatch
findings.claim: The only operation that changes a user's repositories, `handoff merge`, has no reverse path: no revert command, no `merged -> reverted` transition, and no undo on its card. The fate of the implementer's commits and worktrees on `handoff cancel` and `dropped` is not specified. The catalogue's `Undo::NotUndoable(&str)` variant lets any command opt out of reversibility, with no enumerated list and no test that pins it. S15's undo test covers only `Op x target kind` plus review, decision pick, version and claim.
findings.evidence: contracts.md CommandSpec: `undo: Undo, // Edit | Compensate | NotUndoable(&'static str) | Query`. The architecture.md hand-off loop has `merged --> reconciled --> [*]` and no revert state. 'The hand-off loop': merge runs `git merge --no-ff planroom/KEY` in each repo, 'then remove the worktrees'. The `handoff cancel` semantics appear nowhere. The feature_list S15 assert: 'for every Op x target kind, plus review, decision pick, version and claim: apply then undo'. This conflicts with KICKOFF principle 1 ('Never lose or overwrite what someone did. Everything is reversible, which is what makes bold defaults safe').
findings.failure_scenario: A person taps 'merge' on the S4 hand-off. Two repos get merge commits on their default branches, and the worktrees are removed. Reconciliation then shows a regression the person didn't expect. Planroom offers nothing to undo it, so the person has to work out `git revert -m 1` by hand in each repo. Separately, a person who cancels a hand-off to try again may find the implementer's branch and commits gone, which is work lost.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a person-only `handoff revert KEY` that runs `git revert -m 1 <merge>` in each repo behind the same all-or-nothing preflight. Record the pre-merge heads in the `handoff` event. Add a `merged -> reverted` transition to the loop table so S6's own-loop check covers it, and show 'Undo: /room handoff revert KEY' on the merge result and card. On cancel or drop, keep the branch, archived under `refs/planroom/archive/KEY`, and remove only the worktree. Enumerate the `NotUndoable` leaves in the catalogue (`serve`, `watch`, `export`, `share`) with a one-line reason, and add a test that the set equals that list, so a new irreversible command needs a decision record.

findings.title: All user-authored state lives in one untracked, auto-ignored SQLite file with no automatic backup
findings.claim: Plans, the intended architecture, overrides, regroupings, decisions and versions exist only in `WORKSPACE/.planroom/store.db`. That directory carries a `.gitignore` of `*`, and for a single-repo workspace it sits inside the repo's own working tree. DR-34 removed the per-repo export, and `planroom export` is manual. So routine developer actions destroy every person edit with no recovery: `git clean -xfd`, a re-clone, deleting a scratch workspace directory, or a disk issue. This is a data-loss risk under 'never lose what someone did'.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'Where the workspace lives': 'The repos are the root itself if it's a git repo'; '`.planroom/` holds `store.db` ... and a `.gitignore` of `*`'. DR-34: 'the workspace store is the one source; `planroom export` writes events as NDJSON for backup and upgrade'. 'Store schema': 'Only `events` and `ledger` need care across versions, because facts rebuild by rescanning', so events are the irreplaceable part, and nothing copies them automatically. This conflicts with KICKOFF principle 1 ('Never lose or overwrite what someone did') and the data-loss materiality rule. The starting point that DR-34 replaced (a reviewable export) was there partly to give this durability.
findings.failure_scenario: A user plans 'Add retries to the worker' through all seven stages, regroups components and sets intended rules in a single-repo workspace. Later they run `git clean -xfd` to reset build output. `.planroom/` is ignored, so it is deleted. The next `/room` rescans facts but shows an empty plan, no intent and no overrides, with no way to restore them.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the store outside any repo working tree by default (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/planroom/<workspace_id>/`, with `.planroom/` holding only a pointer file), or write a rolling append-only NDJSON event export there automatically. Do the export after every `version` event and person edit batch, and daily, keeping the last N. Make `planroom doctor` and the pane warn when no backup exists. When the store is missing but a backup exists, deal one restore card ('Restore 412 events from Tuesday?', pre-selected Yes). Add a test: run `git clean -xfd` in a single-repo fixture, then `planroom focus`, and the person's edits come back or one restore card appears.

findings.title: The mod pane has no defined content before the engine exists or outside a workspace, and the empty-state audit skips it
findings.claim: Every pane and band row comes from `PaneModel`, produced by `planroom focus --json`, which needs the engine. On first install the engine is downloading, or building from source for about 4 minutes, so the opened pane has no model. When `focus` returns an error envelope (`workspace_not_found` for a directory with no repos, `schema_mismatch`, `store_busy`), the design defines no pane content either. `workspace_not_found` is an error, not an `empty {reason, next}`, so the first-run 'not a workspace yet' case has no next action. S15's empty-state audit only visits canvas views on an empty-git-repo workspace.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'Wiring' step 1: when the engine is missing, the mod shows 'Getting the Planroom engine...' only in the status line. Step 5 opens the pane unasked at ≥110 columns. 'Mod refresh': the pane redraws from the `planroom.pane` atom written by `focus`. Error codes: `workspace_not_found` | not_found | 'no repos at the path'. The feature_list S15 fixture and steps: 'an empty workspace (a directory with one empty git repo)'; 'Playwright: ... every view visited on the empty workspace must render its empty.next action'. Neither the pane nor the CLI is audited. This conflicts with KICKOFF principle 1 ('Never show a blank state'), S15 ('An empty-state screenshot audit finds no blank states'), and the S14 first-run path.
findings.failure_scenario: On S14's fresh install, the person runs `/plugin install` and starts a session in `~/code` (a directory of repos with no `.planroom/`, or no repos at all). The pane docks and stays empty while the engine downloads or builds. Then `focus` returns `workspace_not_found`, and the pane shows a raw error or nothing. The first screen a new user sees is blank.
findings.proposed_fix: Generate a fallback `PaneModel` set into `catalogue.ts` from the engine's `en.toml` (so the strings stay engine-authored) for these states: engine fetching (with progress), engine build offered, not a workspace, store busy, and version mismatch. Each has one primary band action, such as 'Scan this directory', 'Build engine', or 'Pick a repo'. Make `focus` return `ok` with `empty: {reason: no_repos, next: scan .}` instead of an error when no repos are found. Extend the empty-state audit to the pane on all four surfaces through `claude plugin test`, covering each fallback state and each error frame.

findings.title: Plan-stage Claude prefixes are per stage and used once per plan, so caching costs more than it saves
findings.claim: Each plan stage has its own prompt file, and the request prefix is `[pack prompt file] + [output schema]`. So the seven S3 stage calls each use a distinct prefix, and each is written to the cache once and read roughly never. Stages also run at human pace, minutes apart, against a 5-minute TTL (the session backend's `cache: true` is fixed at 5 minutes). The S3 cache-hit rate the budget commits will sit near 0, every stage pays the cache-write premium, and the `cache_regression` alarm only catches rewrites within the TTL, so it never fires. The prefix is stable and marked for caching, but it doesn't cache.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'Claude': 'A request is `[pack prompt file] + [output JSON Schema]`, a cache breakpoint, then `[slice as JSON] + [the question]`'. Pack table: `[[stages]]` has a per-stage `prompt`. 'Planning': 'the engine asks Claude with the stage's cached prefix'. claude-gateway.md: `cache_ttl = "5m"` default, with `ttl:"1h"` supported (line 82). mod-api.md: 'cache: true ... for 5 minutes'. This conflicts with KICKOFF principle 2 ('Claude calls keep a stable, cached prefix'; 'Token-efficient by design') and S7 ('record ... the Claude tokens with their cache-hit rate. Commit those as budgets').
findings.failure_scenario: In the S3 evidence run, a person walks 'Add retries to the worker' through the stages over 15 minutes. Each `intent next --stage S` creates a new cache entry of at least 1,024 tokens at about 1.25x the input price and reads none. The recorded cache-hit rate is about 0, and that becomes the committed budget, so the regression test can never catch a real caching loss.
findings.proposed_fix: Use one plan-pack prefix shared by every stage: all seven methods, the stage table and the union output schema. Put the stage ID and its short instructions in the uncached tail. Apply the same rule to other multi-call purposes: one prefix per pack and role, not per sub-step. Use `ttl: "1h"` on the gateway for human-paced purposes (plan, curate) and 5 minutes for batch purposes (escalations within a decide run). Make `budgets.rs` assert a cache-hit-rate floor for the S3 stage sequence, for example ≥0.6 of prompt tokens after the first stage, not only 'within 0.1 of the last value'.

findings.title: Ghost-only writes still go through permission prompts, so a person is interrupted twice for one proposal
findings.claim: `room_change` writes from an agent are ghosts by construction: inert, excluded from questions, lint and reconciliation, and reversible. Yet the tool goes through 'the normal permission flow'. In default mode, each proposal therefore costs a permission prompt and then a ghost-batch accept. Remote sync is 3 or 4 `ArtifactData` calls that are never auto-allowed, so each sync is several more prompts. These prompts guard actions the person must review anyway.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'Tools' table: `room_change` → 'the normal permission flow'. 'Layers, overrides and ghosts': any agent edit is a ghost until a person's `review accept`. R-5: 'sync is 3 or 4 short calls'. DR-31: the mod 'never auto-allows' `ArtifactData`. This conflicts with KICKOFF principle 1 ('Interrupt a person only for decisions only they can make').
findings.failure_scenario: In S3 through the mod, each of the six stage proposals asks 'Allow mcp__planroom__room_change?' and then deals an 'Accept 5 proposals?' card. That's 12 interruptions where 6 would do, and each `/room sync` adds 3 or 4 more.
findings.proposed_fix: Split `room_change` into a ghost-only, auto-allowed tool (`edit`, `intent` proposals, `claim`, `scan`, `curate`) and a gated one (`import`, `decide --run`, which can apply auto-enabled effects), still within the 1,500-token surface budget. Document the permission rule that pre-allows the two `ArtifactData` calls the sync makes on the Planroom artifact URL, and offer it once as a one-tap card.

findings.title: The retry contract is not machine-readable: a boolean retryable contradicts the registry and DR-7
findings.claim: `ErrorObject.retryable` is a `bool`, but the registry lists values like 'after a re-read' (`stale_write`) and 'later' (`budget_exceeded`). The canonical `stale_write` example sets `retryable: false`, while DR-7 says an agent 're-reads and retries'. An agent that trusts the typed field gives up on exactly the case the design expects it to retry. `model_unavailable` is an error code described as a warning, next to the `deterministic_fallback` warning, which gives one condition two codes.
findings.evidence: contracts.md `ErrorObject { retryable: bool }`; error table rows `stale_write | ... | after a re-read`, `budget_exceeded | ... | later`; JSON example `"code":"stale_write",...,"retryable":false`. architecture.md 'Conflicts': 'The agent re-reads and retries.' This conflicts with KICKOFF principle 2 ('stable, typed, documented interfaces, with stable error codes').
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer or curator agent gets `stale_write` with `retryable:false` and stops, reporting failure, instead of re-reading `meta.seq` and retrying. The design's intended agent recovery path fails silently, and S8-style agent races leave work stuck in 'agent retries'.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace `retryable: bool` with `retry: "never" | "now" | "after_reread" | "later"`, plus an optional `retry_after_ms`, and generate it into `errors.md` from the registry. Keep `model_unavailable` as an error only, and use `deterministic_fallback` as the one warning for that condition. Extend `the_documented_error_table_is_the_error_codes` to cover the retry class.

findings.title: The turn-start remote-sync line has no stated injection point and could break the cached system prefix
findings.claim: Remote mode adds 'a turn-start context line when remote mode is on and the last sync is more than 10 minutes old'. The design guarantees that the `prompt.compose` section is byte-identical across turns, but it never says where this conditional, time-dependent line goes. If it is added through `prompt.compose`, the chat's cached prefix changes whenever remote mode or sync age flips.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'Remote mode' step 6 (the turn-start context line); 'Prompt section': 'identical across turns, so it stays in the cached prefix [DR-20]'. mod-api.md §: `prompt.compose` adds a system-prompt section, and `prompt.context` adds blocks only on the first message. This conflicts with KICKOFF principle 2 ('Claude calls keep a stable, cached prefix').
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer puts the hint in the composed `planroom` section. Every turn after 10 minutes without a sync, and every sync, changes the system prompt, and the chat model re-writes its whole cached prefix (tools, skills, system), multiplying the chat session's input cost.
findings.proposed_fix: State that dynamic hints go only into the band, the status line or per-turn user-side context, never into the composed system section. Add a mod test that the composed section is byte-identical with remote mode on and off and across sync ages.

findings.title: Agent defaults are not agent-first: text without --json, and focus carries the minimap to agents
findings.claim: A non-TTY CLI call, the agent case, defaults to text unless `--json` is passed, though the design already detects non-TTY callers to set the actor. `room_query focus` returns the full `PaneModel`, including up to 60 mini-map blocks, which an agent never uses, inside a 1,000-token budget. The session-backend reply gives an agent no defined way to get the result once the mod has fulfilled the request: it has to re-run the command, with no handle or notification.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'The CLI': 'text output is the rendered summary'; Actors: no-TTY means an agent. contracts.md `PaneModel.minimap: MiniMap // up to 60 blocks`. The `room_query` leaves include `focus`. The 'Claude' session backend: 're-running the command picks it up'. This conflicts with KICKOFF principle 2 ('Output is designed for agents first ... compact'; 'summary-first, with handles').
findings.failure_scenario: An agent in a session without mods runs `planroom ask unmonitored` through Bash, forgets `--json`, and parses prose. A chat agent polls `focus` and pays about 400 tokens of mini-map per call. After `intent next` returns `model_request_pending`, the agent loops on re-running the command and spends turns.
findings.proposed_fix: Default to the JSON envelope when stdout is not a TTY, and keep text for TTYs and an explicit `--text`. Give agent-facing `focus` a `--detail summary` default without `minimap` and `who` rows beyond the top 3. Make a pending session-backend reply carry `meta.next` as the exact re-run handle, and have the mod, after `import`, post the completed result into the turn so the agent doesn't poll.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed and minor. The turn-start sync hint has no stated injection point. The mod's registered hooks include `prompt.compose`, but not `prompt.context` or `turn.start`. `prompt.context` only adds blocks on the first message, and `turn.start` is observe-only, so `prompt.compose` is the only prompt hook the design registers. An implementer could well put the time-dependent line there and break the byte-identical cached section.

verdicts.reason: Real and minor, and partly mitigated. A non-TTY CLI call defaults to text even though the engine already detects non-TTY callers to set the actor. `PaneModel` carries the minimap to agents.
